sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house in Goodyear, AZ?
sections.html:
A Goodyear homeowner can list the house on the open market, sell it without an agent, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the property in its present condition. The cash route usually closes sooner because it skips repairs, showings and a buyer's loan approval. The listing route can produce a higher price when the house is in good order and there is time to wait.

  • Open-market listing: the best fit for a recently updated house in a master-planned community with an active homeowners association.
  • Cash purchase as-is: the best fit for a house with deferred maintenance, a vacant property, or an inherited home that the heirs want to close out.
  • Sale by owner: the best fit for owners who already know the local price range and can manage the paperwork.

Goodyear is one of the fastest-growing places in the Phoenix area. The Census Bureau counts 125,359 residents on July 1, 2025, up 30.4% from the April 2020 base of 96,141. Owners hold 77.7% of occupied homes, and the median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $471,300.

sections.h2: What is Goodyear like, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Goodyear is a city in Maricopa County about 17 miles west of downtown Phoenix, and its 191 square miles of land make it far larger than most neighbors. Avondale, Litchfield Park, Tolleson and Buckeye lie nearby, and the northern edge meets Glendale. The Gila River crosses the city, and the Estrella Mountains rise near its southern communities.

The Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company started the settlement in 1917 by buying 16,000 acres to grow cotton for tire cord. Goodyear became a town on November 19, 1946 and a city in 1985, and in 1987 the last 10,000 acres of company farmland were sold for future development. Most of the building happened after 1990. Estrella, south of the Gila River, is the largest master-planned community at about 20,000 acres, Palm Valley lies north of Interstate 10, and PebbleCreek is built for active adults. Goodyear Ballpark hosts spring training for the Cleveland Guardians and the Cincinnati Reds.

Because so many Goodyear homes sit inside planned communities, an HOA often shapes what a seller can do. The city's own code compliance page says some neighborhood rules, such as parking limits, come from private covenants enforced by an association instead of city code. Summer highs reach 100 degrees or more through June, July and August, with roughly ten inches of rain a year. Workers in Goodyear report a mean commute of 29.6 minutes.

sections.h2: Which Goodyear code rules can affect a sale?
sections.html:
Goodyear's Code Compliance Division responds to complaints about property that can be seen from the public right of way, so a seller should walk the front and sides of the house the way an inspector or neighbor would. Cases usually take 30 to 45 days to resolve, and a notice typically allows 10 to 30 days to fix a violation. The division can be reached at 623-882-7815 or codecompliance@goodyearaz.gov.

  • Weeds and grass on residential lots must stay under six inches and cannot hang over a sidewalk.
  • Recreational vehicles, boats and trailers belong in a garage or a paved side or rear yard behind a solid six foot fence, and no more than two may be stored there.
  • No more than four household pets are allowed per property.
  • Front yard fences top out at three feet and rear yard fences at six feet, and fences under six feet generally need no building permit.
  • Trash and recycling containers stay out of view of the street except on collection days.

The city notes that violations on vacant and foreclosed homes can take months or longer to resolve because owners are hard to locate. If a Goodyear house sits empty, keep the yard cleared and a mailing address on file with the county so notices reach you.

sections.h2: Do Goodyear permits and building codes matter when selling?
sections.html:
Yes. Goodyear's homeowner guidance says all plan submittals and inspections must follow the adopted building codes, amendments and ordinances, including sound mitigation. Permitted work has to remain exposed for inspection, so ask the city whether past projects on the house, such as a pool, patio cover or addition, have a closed permit.

The city's EZ Permit lane covers minor jobs such as a residential pool or spa built from approved standard plans, and those permits are reviewed within five business days. Larger jobs, such as an addition or a detached accessory structure, go through the regular residential submittal guides on the Development Resources page. Questions go to the Building Safety Division at 623-932-3004 or buildingsafety@goodyearaz.gov. Check your HOA covenants as well, because the city says the owner, not the city, is responsible for knowing them before any modification.

sections.h2: What should Goodyear owners know about rentals and short-term stays?
sections.html:
A Goodyear owner who rents out the house must register it with the Maricopa County Assessor under A.R.S. 33-1902, and the city says failing to register carries a mandatory civil penalty of $1,000 plus $100 for each additional month. Goodyear also adopted a Residential Rental Property Ordinance, Article 11-1-21, that sets minimum health and safety standards for the interior and exterior of any apartment, single-family home or mobile home rented for a fee.

Short stays are handled separately. Goodyear's Finance Department runs a short-term rental licensing program with its own application requirements, listing requirements, annual renewal and an emergency and complaint contact record that owners keep current. The Finance Department's short-term rental desk is at 1900 N Civic Square, reachable at str@goodyearaz.gov or 623-882-7887 option 4. State law in A.R.S. 9-500.39 prevents a city from banning short-term rentals, though it permits licensing, zoning and safety rules.

sections.h2: How do taxes, appeals and recording work for a Goodyear sale?
sections.html:
Goodyear property taxes are collected by Maricopa County. Half is due October 1 and half March 1, and A.R.S. 42-18052 makes the first half delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second half after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. The county's calendar shows November 2, 2026 as this year's first-half delinquency date, and it has passed. Ask your escrow officer to confirm what remains unpaid and how the year's tax will be split at closing.

  • The Assessor's Notice of Value arrives between January 1 and March 1, and a petition is due 60 days after the mailing date.
  • The Assessor must answer by August 15, and the State Board of Equalization hears the next level.
  • Taxes follow the limited property value, which can rise by only 5% a year barring new construction or a change of use, and only the full cash value can be appealed.

The deed is recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder, whose office says it cannot advise on legal documents and directs customers to a title company or attorney. A completed affidavit of value goes with the deed unless an exemption from A.R.S. 11-1134, such as a gift deed, is written on its face.

faqs.q: Can the city of Goodyear fine me for yard or storage violations before I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Code Compliance can issue a notice and, if the problem continues, a civil citation that is a summons to appear in court, where a fine can be imposed. Typical correction periods run from 10 to 30 days, and the city can be reached at 623-882-7815.

Yes, with a city license. Goodyear's Finance Department runs the licensing program, owners keep emergency and complaint contacts on file, and State law bars cities from prohibiting short-term rentals. Licensing questions go to str@goodyearaz.gov.

faqs.q: How many pets and recreational vehicles can I keep at a Goodyear house?
faqs.a: Goodyear limits households to four pets, and it lets a property store no more than two recreational vehicles, trailers or boats in the side or rear yard, on a paved surface behind a solid six foot fence.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Goodyear?
faqs.a: Generally not for fences under six feet, but exceptions can apply. Front yard fences may reach three feet and rear yard fences six feet. Call the Development Counter at 623-932-3004 before building.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Goodyear home?
faqs.a: Half is due October 1 and half is due March 1. The first half turns delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second after 5:00 p.m. on May 1, with Maricopa County listing November 2 for 2026 because November 1 fell on a Sunday.
